messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT 1755550000 - Elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (us-east-1). Error pattern: SIGSEGV in model-runner. See runbook: https://go/runbooks/runtime-segfault. Paging on-call.

ashley: oncall here. seeing spike on the dashboard — 5xx ~18% over last 3m, tail latency up. any initial clues?

jules: I'm on it. I can reproduce segfaults in model-runner logs on a subset of nodes (p3.*). stack trace shows mem access violation in kv_cache.c around LRU eviction. attaching snippet below.

jules: ```
[model-runner][pid=3245] SIGSEGV at 0x7f8b3f2a
#0 0x7f8b3f2a in kv_cache_evict+0x12b
#1 0x7f8b5a4c in model_step+0x3f2
#2 0x7f8b6cde in infer_loop+0x81
```

robin: copying perf + OOM counters: memory usage for model-worker processes trending to 98% before crash. Paging events spike right before SIGSEGV. Could be double-free after eviction.

emma: product here — what's the customer impact? is any SLA breached or major account affected? need numbers for comms.

miguel: support: 7 open tickets flagged as "generate failure" in last 10m, 2 marked P1 from AcmeCorp (they're hitting the streaming endpoint). Customers seeing HTTP 502/503 timeouts. Sending sample request IDs to SRE.

leo: infra: looks like GPU nodes with kernel 5.15 show coredump rate higher. Suggest draining affected hosts and routing traffic away. Commands: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-42 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets gpu-node-42` then move workloads via routing policy.

ashley: let's do mitigation plan A (fast): 1) enable fallback to smaller quantized model (q4_k_m) for /v1/generate via routing policy, 2) route traffic for AcmeCorp to dedicated pool with reserved capacity, 3) drain suspected hosts. Anyone object?

jules: +1 for fallback. We should also lower max_batch_size to 1 on the affected model to reduce memory pressure: `rbctl model update --id model-llama-7b --max-batch-size 1`. Applying now to canary.

deploy-bot: deploy started: model-config update model-llama-7b (max_batch_size=1) by jules at 1755550330.

jules: canary looks good on 10k requests, no segfaults so far. rolling config to remaining replica set.

robin: adding temporary kernel parameter to suppress aggressive page reclaim: `echo 1200 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_writeback_centisecs` (note: short-lived). Also increasing OOM score for sidecars.

leo: drained 3 nodes and evicted pods. migrating traffic to dedicated-01 pool. Made sure dedicated pool has headroom: +4 instances launched.

emma: ETA for full mitigation? we need to tell CS and account teams.

miguel: AcmeCorp requests still failing at ~1 in 20. after routing to dedicated-01 their error rate dropped to ~2%. passing that to Acme account rep.

jules: got a core dump from model-worker on gpu-node-42. grabbing gdb backtrace now. early look suggests corrupted free list in kv_cache after concurrent eviction + async prefetch.

jules: ```
#0 0x7f8b3f2a in kv_cache_evict+0x12b
(gdb) bt
#0 kv_cache_evict
#1 model_step
#2 infer_loop
#3 start_thread
#4 __clone
```

robin: can we quick patch to disable async prefetch in the runtime? a config toggle would be safest. If not, revert code path to sync only.

jules: I can flip `runtime.async_prefetch=false` in configstore and roll across nodes. Doing that now for canary.

deploy-bot: config update runtime.async_prefetch=false by jules at 1755550720.

jules: async_prefetch=false canary = stable on 10 nodes. no segfaults observed in the next 5 minutes. rolling to fleet.

ashley: status check: 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 3% cluster-wide; tail latency improving. still monitoring AcmeCorp but their traffic routed to dedicated pool which is healthy.

emma: thanks — sending comms to affected customers: "We experienced elevated errors on /v1/generate due to runtime crashes. Traffic has been routed to a safe fallback and we are rolling a mitigation. We'll post a postmortem."

miguel: I told Acme support the temporary mitigation and that a deeper fix is coming. they're OK for now but want root cause and ETA.

leo: for follow-up infra work: will repro on an isolated machine with kernel 5.15 and run valgrind/asan to validate double-free. open infra ticket INFRA-4321.

jules: plan for code fix: guard around kv_cache_evict and add unit test and concurrency invariant. I'll open a PR and request expedited review. linking PR when ready.

robin: also scheduling a rolling restart of all model-runner pods once code fix lands (canary first). we should add a liveness probe backoff so we don't thrash.

ashley: handing off to jules for next 8h. summary: initial SIGSEGVs causing 5xx spike (~18%), mitigation = fallback to quantized model + disable async prefetch + drain affected nodes + route major customers to dedicated pool. Current cluster 5xx ~2.8%. customer P1s reduced to 0.

ashley: next oncall (tom) pls pick up at 1755551800. creating incident ticket: INC-175555. postmortem owner: jules.

jules: taking handoff. I'll post follow-ups (PR link, postmortem) in INC-175555.

deploy-bot: incident closed by ashley at 1755551795 (mitigation active, monitoring).

ashley: thanks team. follow-up items: PR + test, infra repro + kernel alignment, postmortem + customer comms.

emma: noted — I'll sync with comms & account teams.

miguel: closing related support tickets once fix deployed.

robin: I'll add runtime metrics alert to detect this pattern earlier (kv eviction + paging events) and a runbook step to enable fallback automatically if >10% 5xx for 5m.

jules: link to incident: https://go/incidents/INC-175555. PR opened: https://go/pull/rlw/987 (WIP).

ashley: handoff complete. ending thread."
